clue.text: Measuring device for tower

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
a tractor is something that tows, read as tow-er

explanation.surface: A surveyor's instrument for measuring a tall tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' looks like a tall building, but here it is one who tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometry instrument used for measuring angles is a straightforward example of a measuring device.

clue.text: Blade theologian used in fencing

indicators.note: used in means the theologian letters are placed within the fencing word

parts.note: a pale is a stake in a fence, and fencing as a whole
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian wields a blade in a fencing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests swordplay with a blade, but it is a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar or a canoe's oar is called its blade.

clue.text: Old cooker in Dutch house

parts.note: a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: An old stove stands in a house in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal family is the House of Orange-Nassau, a ruling dynasty.

clue.text: A dictator there in revolt to make drastic threat

indicators.note: in revolt suggests upheaval, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A dictator faced with an uprising issues a severe warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an old British law read aloud to disperse crowds; the idiom means to give a stern warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for scolding someone severely and warning them of consequences.

clue.text: Tea for every single person giving protection

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
per means for each, as in per person
one means single

explanation.surface: Tea for each lone person, offered as protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an escort who accompanies and guards a young person.

clue.text: Love unchanged spot that's pleasant

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: A beloved place remains unspoilt and pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven of green and water in a desert, figuratively any welcome refuge.

clue.text: Bookie's offer about to finish

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first piece wraps the word to

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds a bookmaker offers at the off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds are about to close for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The starting price is the odds a bookmaker pays at the moment a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to a halt or end is a plain synonym of finishing it.

clue.text: After time, I tucked into slice of bacon of worse quality

indicators.note: after means the bacon piece comes later, following the time letter
tucked into means the letter goes inside the bacon word

parts.note: a rasher is a thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: After a while, I tucked into some poor-quality bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of trashy, rubbishy or cheap, so meaning lower quality.

clue.text: English trade union in factory with bad attitude

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: An English union in a factory shows a bad attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sulky and childishly bad-tempered is having a poor attitude.

clue.text: Sit around in costume trousers from the Seventies, things for an emergency

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the costume word

parts.note: dress means costume, as in fancy dress

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: flares are wide-bottomed trousers fashionable in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Lounging in fancy dress and Seventies flares, waiting for an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but scrambles the three letters, making IST; 'in' then does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal rockets fired to call for rescue are things kept for emergencies.

clue.text: Martial arts expert goes round island with a girl

indicators.note: goes round means the first piece encloses the letter for island

parts.note: a dan is a graded expert in judo or karate

explanation.surface: A judo black belt travels round an island with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, as in Princess Diana, so the female name stands for girl.

clue.text: Attacker from South America, one coming in at an angle

indicators.note: coming in means these pieces are placed inside the word for at an angle

parts.note: aslant means slanting or at an angle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A raider from South America swoops in on a slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assaults or attacks someone is a direct synonym of an attacker.

clue.text: Person who's left something on a support

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the side where the batsman stands
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Someone has left something lying on a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' suggests departing, but it means bequeathed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone named in a will to receive a bequest is literally a person something was left to.

clue.text: Bag carried by gardeners at Chelsea

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bag toted around by gardeners at the Chelsea Flower Show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chelsea Flower Show is a famous London gardening event.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder bag of the kind schoolchildren carry is one type of bag.

clue.text: Become used to batting yet seeing one beaten

indicators.note: beaten suggests something battered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batsman is still getting the hang of it, yet sees a team-mate beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who has settled in and judges the ball well has got their eye in.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from cricket for settling in at the crease and adjusting to the bowling.

clue.text: Reckons big cars will go about one mile

indicators.note: will go about means the car word goes round the other letters

parts.note: estates are estate cars, roomy vehicles with a rear hatch
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone reckons large cars will travel about a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate cars are what Americans call station wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon or calculate roughly, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Jubilant financial district staying put

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
static means not moving

explanation.surface: The financial district celebrates while standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode covering the City, its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Overjoyed and thrilled, a direct synonym of jubilant.

clue.text: Fish as start of meal adorned with chopped parsley

indicators.note: adorned with means the first letter is surrounded by the garnish letters
chopped suggests cutting up, so the herb's letters are rearranged
start of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Fish served as a starter, garnished with chopped parsley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' turns PARSLEY into LAPREYS, which goes round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Eel-like jawless creatures that suck blood are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Musician performing in recitals not drinking therein

indicators.note: therein means the teetotal letters go inside the rearranged letters
performing suggests putting on a show, here working the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
TT means teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A performer at recitals stays sober throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' scrambles the fodder into CLARINEIST; 'therein' means the teetotal pair sits within that result.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a woodwind instrument is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Again sound out Greek character about forerunner of EU

indicators.note: about means the Greek letter goes round the community letters

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the EEC, European Economic Community, preceded the European Union

explanation.surface: A Greek figure speaks again about the EU's predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound or reverberate again, repeating a sound a second time.

clue.text: Yard beneath shop floor

indicators.note: beneath means the yard letter sits under the shop word in this down clue

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A yard lies under the floor of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: One level of a building, as in the third floor, is a synonym.

clue.text: Means to attract attention in row — I'll give better advice

indicators.note: in means the sound goes inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
pst is the hissing sound used to get someone's notice

explanation.surface: Someone in a row hisses to get noticed, claiming superior advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is not 'superior' but one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tout offers betting suggestions to punters, so they advise gamblers.

clue.text: Stretch of river for everyone

parts.note: each means for every one, as in five pounds each

explanation.surface: A stretch of river open to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch of river' reads as one phrase, a river reach, but the definition is only 'Stretch'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an arm out is to stretch, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Most gentle criminal 'Slim Ted'

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A crook nicknamed Slim Ted is the gentlest of the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of mild, meaning softest or least harsh, which matches most gentle.

clue.text: Cutting ditch needs worker perhaps

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch
a worker is one kind of ant, so ant is an example

explanation.surface: Digging a ditch needs a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like digging, but it is the adjective for sharp remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is incisive and sharp, the same sense as a biting comment.

clue.text: Regarding vehicle turning over, it goes very fast

indicators.note: turning over means the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A report about a vehicle overturning at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built for speed competitions, like a fast car or horse, moves very quickly.

clue.text: Cover mathematical function of variable

parts.note: cos is short for cosine, a trigonometric function
y is a typical variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Covering a mathematical function of a variable.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover for a teapot or boiled egg, a tea warmer, is called this.

clue.text: Good entertainer's right person to provide scary tale

parts.note: a host entertains guests; the possessive gives the s
a Tory is a right-winger, a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A fine entertainer is the right person to tell a spooky tale.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: A spooky story about spirits is the classic scary tale told round the fire.
